title: Nehai the Arbelite (name as supplied)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Yehoshua ben Perachya’s av beit din (head of the court). They received the tradition from the Pairs: Yose ben Yoezer of Tzereida and Yose ben Yochanan of Jerusalem, as in Avot, chapter 1, mishnayot 6 and 7. His precious saying remains with us: “Keep far from a bad neighbor, do not associate with a wicked person, and do not despair of retribution.”[^2]
In Chagigah, chapter 2, mishnah 2, he disagrees with Yehoshua ben Perachya about laying hands on an offering on a festival, and says that one should lay hands.[^3]

notes.text: The native page and the supplied proofread heading read נהאי הארבלי, rendered provisionally as Nehai the Arbelite. The source filename and retained machine transcription instead have נתאי (Nittai). This note preserves the printed form; it does not identify or merge the two names.

The native line reads הוא היה האב״ד דיהושע בן פרחיה, supporting “He was Yehoshua ben Perachya’s av beit din.” The retained machine transcription instead reads ויהושע (“and Yehoshua”). The supplied Hebrew is unchanged. Hyman uses the plural הזוגות, “the Pairs,” before the two names. The Avot references and the maxim remain Hyman’s report, not independently checked passages.

Av beit din expands אב״ד in its ordinary sense; ב״פ is understood from the earlier full name בן פרחיה, and יו״ט means a festival. The English rendering of the ruling follows Hyman. No new personal title, identity binding or independent citation verification is implied.
